title: Customer tuning intake: SLA‑weighted prioritization lattice for optimization requests
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers and platform teams submit inbound requests for performance tuning (batch sizing, KV/prefix cache configuration, quantization profile recommendations, and routing policy adjustments). Currently these requests arrive via email/Slack and are handled ad hoc by solutions engineers, which causes inconsistent prioritization, long response times, and missed SLA expectations for Dedicated/Private customers.

Goal: Define and ship an SLA‑aware intake + prioritization lattice (scoring system + lanes + handoff playbook) to route optimization/advisory requests to the right responder (self-serve docs, concierge, eng consult, or escalation to reliability). The system should be deterministic, auditable, and simple enough for solutions engineers and success managers to apply during a 15‑minute intake call.

Scope: Non-bug optimization/advisory requests only (performance/cost/quality tuning that does not require code changes). Includes batching/caching knobs, quantization profiles, model routing policies, and configuration recommendations. Excludes production incidents and feature requests requiring product changes.
acceptance_criteria: A public intake form (hosted in Confluence + webhook to Zendesk) captures structured signals: customer SLOs, affected endpoints, token volume, current latency/cost, privacy/regulatory constraints, and requested outcome.
A 6‑factor SLA‑weighted scoring formula implemented in a lightweight scoring sheet and an automated triage lambda that returns lane: self-serve | concierge | eng-consult | reliability-escalation.
Runbook for concierge lane with clear TATs (2 business days), required artifacts, and success metrics; handoff checklist to eng when technical change is needed.
Dashboard that surfaces incoming optimization signal volume, median time-to-first-response, and distribution across lanes; baseline created within 2 weeks of rollout.

Pilot with 3 enterprise customers (one Dedicated, two Private) and three internal SEs completed, with retrospective recorded and <=15% manual reclassifications from initial scoring during pilot period.
